userStories.title: Catalog: agent prompts and agent lookup; /plugins wording
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Retain agent prompt bodies and make every catalog agent discoverable using existing precedence and qualified lookup.

**Motivation** — Claude Code users keep reviewers, planners and researchers as agent files; today `/plugins` prints `agents N (not delivered yet)` and the chat model has no way to use them.

**Approach** — `AgentResource` gains `prompt: string`: the agent file's body without frontmatter, read the way `parseSkillFile` reads `SkillResource.body`. `ResourceCatalog` gains `agents` (every loaded agent in package order, shadowed ones included) and `findAgent(name)`, built by the same `indexResources` precedence as skills and commands (project > user > plugin; a shadowed agent stays reachable as `<plugin>:<name>`; a shadow adds the existing warn diagnostic `<kind> <name> from <pkg> is shadowed by <winner>; use <qualifiedName>` with kind `agent`). `formatPluginsListing` stops printing `(not delivered yet)` after the agents count; the hooks `(not executed)` wording stays. The `parseAgentFile` doc comment stops saying the body is not retained.

**Scope** — In: resource types, agent parser, catalog indexes, plugins listing, existing parser/listing fixtures and fixture-repository loading tests. Out: agent invocation (US-006/007), model/tool mapping (US-004), /agents formatting (US-011). Agents are not hot-reloaded; a changed agent file takes effect at the next `nax chat` start. Hooks stay parsed and listed as not executed.

**Interface** — `AgentResource` gains `prompt: string`; `ResourceCatalog` gains `agents` and `findAgent(name)`.

Required existing test updates: the two whole-resource toEqual expectations in test/unit/resources/parse-agent.test.ts gain prompt equal to their fixture body; rename "qualifies plugin agents without retaining executable body" to "qualifies plugin agents and retains the prompt body". Every name, description, model and tools expectation is unchanged. The two agent literals in test/unit/resources/listing.test.ts gain prompt: ""; change only "agents 2 (not delivered yet)" to "agents 2" in the sp@m listing expectation. Extend existing catalog.test.ts for loadResourceCatalog over a real .claude/agents fixture. Preserve all other listing wording and resource discovery behavior.

userStories.title: Config: agent.modelAliases
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add validated Claude Code model aliases with backward-compatible empty defaults on both config parsing paths.

**Motivation** — User ruling 2026-10-25: keep the `haiku`/`sonnet`/`opus` to `models.native` tier step, with an alias always winning.

**Approach** — A new config map from a Claude Code model name to a nax model id, default `{}`. Each value must be a nax model id the way `parseNativeModel` reads one: a non-empty provider before the first `/`, a non-empty remainder after it, no whitespace, an optional `[effort]` suffix (`openrouter/z-ai/glm-5.3-flash[high]` is valid). Four places change: `AgentConfigSchema` (`schemas-infra.ts`), the explicit `agent` default literal in `NaxConfigSchema` (`schemas.ts`, which Zod returns unparsed, so it must carry `modelAliases: {}`), the hand-written `AgentConfig` interface (`runtime-types-agent.ts`, `modelAliases?: Readonly<Record<string, string>>`), and the config descriptions registry (`agent.modelAliases`).

**Scope** — In: the four config surfaces and existing agent/config schema tests. Out: runtime alias precedence and native tier resolution (US-004), host application (US-009), listing resolved models (US-011). A per-agent model or tool override inside chat is not added; the agent file and `agent.modelAliases` are the switches.

**Interface** — `modelAliases?: Readonly<Record<string, string>>`.

Validate shape without resolving provider catalogs; accept model remainders containing additional slashes and optional effort suffixes. Include modelAliases in validation issue paths. Existing configs need no migration, and unrelated agent defaults must remain unchanged.

userStories.title: Subagent model and tool resolution
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Implement pure model precedence and Claude Code tool-name translation for subagents.

**Motivation** — User ruling 2026-10-25: keep the `haiku`/`sonnet`/`opus` to `models.native` tier step, with an alias always winning.

**Approach** — `resolveSubagentModel` (new, `src/chat/subagent-model.ts`) takes `{ requested?: string; parentModel: string; aliases: Readonly<Record<string, string>>; tiers: NaxConfig["models"]["native"] }` and returns `{ model: string; source: "inherit" | "alias" | "tier" | "model" | "fallback" }` as an ordered pipeline; the first step that answers wins:

1. `requested` absent or `"inherit"` -> the parent's model, source `inherit`.
2. `aliases[requested]` defined -> that value, source `alias`.
3. `requested` is `haiku`, `sonnet` or `opus` and `tiers.fast`, `.balanced` or `.powerful` respectively is configured -> that tier's model (a string entry as is, an object entry as `provider/model`), source `tier`.
4. `requested` contains `/` -> `requested` itself, source `model`.
5. Otherwise -> the parent's model, source `fallback`.

`mapSubagentTools` (new, `src/chat/subagent-tools.ts`) turns an agent's Claude Code `tools:` list into `allowedTools` for US-001, returning `{ allowedTools?: string[]; dropped: { name: string; reason: string }[] }`:

| Agent `tools:` entry | `allowedTools` entry |
|---|---|
| `Read`, `Write`, `Edit`, `Bash`, `Glob`, `Grep`, `Git`, `Delete`, `GitCommit` | the same name |
| `MultiEdit` | `Edit` |
| `Skill` | `nax-skills__*` |
| `mcp__<server>__<tool>` | `<server>__<tool>` |
| `mcp__<server>` | `<server>__*` |
| `Agent`, `Task` | dropped, reason `subagents cannot start subagents` |
| `<Name>(<pattern>)`, for example `Bash(git diff:*)` | the bare `<Name>` mapped by the rows above; the pattern is not enforced |
| anything else | dropped, reason `no nax equivalent` |

`tools:` absent -> no `allowedTools` key (the agent inherits every tool the parent session offers, minus the agents provider). Entries are de-duplicated in first-seen order. A list whose entries are all dropped yields `allowedTools: []` (scratchpad tools only). Both functions are exported from `@/chat`.

**Scope** — In: two pure helper modules, barrel exports and focused unit tests. Out: backend admission filtering (US-001), config validation (US-003), invoking the helpers from host runs (US-009), /agents display (US-011). A Claude Code tool pattern such as `Bash(git diff:*)` is not enforced; the entry grants the whole tool and the existing guarded asks still apply to every call. Claude Code plugin MCP tool names of the form `mcp__plugin_<plugin>_<server>__<tool>` are not translated to nax's `<plugin>-<server>` server ids; such an entry maps to `plugin_<plugin>_<server>__<tool>` and matches nothing.

**Interface** — `resolveSubagentModel` takes `{ requested?: string; parentModel: string; aliases: Readonly<Record<string, string>>; tiers: NaxConfig["models"]["native"] }` and returns `{ model: string; source: "inherit" | "alias" | "tier" | "model" | "fallback" }`; `mapSubagentTools` returns `{ allowedTools?: string[]; dropped: { name: string; reason: string }[] }`.

These helpers must be cost-blind and perform no session creation or provider discovery.

userStories.title: Prompt builders for agents and subagents
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Build agent discovery and nested-session prompts while preserving existing chat and skills output exactly.

**Motivation** — Claude Code users keep reviewers, planners and researchers as agent files; today `/plugins` prints `agents N (not delivered yet)` and the chat model has no way to use them.

**Approach** — New `src/prompts/builders/agents-builder.ts`, exported from `src/prompts/index.ts`:

- `buildAgentsInstructions(agents)`: a first line telling the model to call `nax-agents__run` with an agent name and a self-contained task, then one line `- <qualifiedName>: <description>` per agent. Descriptions are cleaned exactly like the skills index (whitespace runs collapsed to one space, control characters removed, truncated to 200 characters), and at most 150 agents are listed, then `- ... and <N> more`. The cleaning is shared by moving it into an exported helper `cleanIndexDescription(text)` in the skills builder, used by both.
- `buildSubagentInstructions({ agent, mode, rulesIndex })`: the permission paragraph for `mode`, the rules index section (`buildRulesIndexSection`, as chat uses it), then the agent's `prompt` last. The permission sentences move out of `buildChatInstructions` into an exported `chatPermissionParagraph(mode)` in `chat-builder.ts`, which both builders call; `buildChatInstructions`' output is unchanged.

**Scope** — In: shared pure prompt helpers, new agents builder, prompts exports, new builder tests and unchanged existing prompt regressions. Out: provider schemas/execution (US-006), session options/rule lookup (US-007), rule-delivery roles (US-008).

**Interface** — `buildAgentsInstructions(agents)`; `buildSubagentInstructions({ agent, mode, rulesIndex })`; `cleanIndexDescription(text)`; `chatPermissionParagraph(mode)`.

Retain the skills builder's exact cleaning order, including its second space collapse after control removal. Keep the complete existing buildChatInstructions output byte-identical in both modes; extract the permission sentences without adding agent instructions to normal chat. chatPermissionParagraph returns the mode's sentence, not the heading: buildChatInstructions retains its existing ## Permission mode heading and sandbox paragraph. Freeze regression expected strings from the current builders rather than computing expected values through the newly extracted helpers. The negative path is control-character removal from an advertised agent description, not an invented rejection of valid empty prompts. Read rules-index-builder for shownAutomatically composition. Existing skills-builder.test.ts and chat-builder.test.ts must stay green unchanged.

userStories.title: The nax-agents provider
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Expose validated named-agent invocation through a static tool provider and protect its namespace from MCP collisions.

**Motivation** — Claude Code users keep reviewers, planners and researchers as agent files; today `/plugins` prints `agents N (not delivered yet)` and the chat model has no way to use them.

**Approach** — `createAgentsProvider({ catalog, run })` (new, `src/chat/agents-provider.ts`) returns a `static` `ToolProvider` with id `nax-agents`, `stages: ["*"]`, and one tool `run` (the model sees `nax-agents__run`) whose input schema is `{ agent: string, task: string }`, both required, `additionalProperties: false`. Its `tools()` returns `[]` when the catalog has no agents. Its `instructions()` returns `buildAgentsInstructions(catalog.agents)`, or `undefined` with no agents. `run` validates its input (both strings, both non-empty after trimming), looks the agent up with `catalog.findAgent`, and calls the injected `run(agent, task, signal)` with `ToolRunContext.signal`, returning its `ToolResult`. The provider id is reserved: `createChatMcp` drops an MCP server whose id is `nax-agents` with the same reserved-id diagnostic it gives `nax-skills` today (the single `RESERVED_SERVER_ID` becomes a set of both ids).

**Scope** — In: agents-provider, MCP reserved-id filtering and diagnostics, provider tests and prompt/catalog seams. Out: nested session lifecycle (US-007/008), host attachment and asks (US-009), usage/cost forwarding (US-010). Subagents in `nax run` are not supported; the agents provider attaches to `nax chat` only.

**Interface** — `createAgentsProvider({ catalog, run })` returns a `ToolProvider`; injected `run(agent, task, signal)` returns its `ToolResult`.

Failure results are exact: missing/non-string/trim-empty agent or task returns `{ isError: true, content: "[chat] run requires agent: string and task: string" }` without calling the runner. Unknown names return `unknown agent <name>; available: <up to 20 qualified names, comma-separated>`. Use catalog order for available names. Preserve the injected result unchanged and pass the context signal through. The US-002 -> US-006 seam uses a catalog built by buildResourceCatalog and proves the runner receives the parsed agent prompt, including qualified shadowed lookup. The US-005 -> US-006 seam checks provider instructions contain the catalog agent line. Keep the existing nax-skills reserved-id diagnostic unchanged.

userStories.title: /agents
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Expose catalog agents, resolved models and mapped/dropped tools through the native host and a built-in /agents command.

**Motivation** — Claude Code users keep reviewers, planners and researchers as agent files; today `/plugins` prints `agents N (not delivered yet)` and the chat model has no way to use them.

**Approach** — `ChatAgentRow` (in `src/chat/chat-agents-listing.ts`, exported from `@/chat`) is `{ name, description, model, modelSource, tools: readonly string[] | "all", dropped }`. `ChatHost.agents?(): readonly ChatAgentRow[]` returns one row per catalog agent in catalog order, resolved against the chat session's current model. `formatAgentsListing(rows)` prints one line per agent `<name>  <model> (<modelSource>)  tools <comma list, "all", or "none">  <description>` (description cleaned by `cleanIndexDescription`), then an indented line `  dropped: <name> (<reason>)` per dropped tool; with no rows it prints `(no agents)`. `/agents` is a built-in slash command between `/mcp` and `/quit`.

**Scope** — In: listing row/formatter, native host agents(), chat barrel exports, slash-command routing/help order, empty optional-host fallback and focused formatter/host/UI seams. Out: model/tool resolver changes (US-004), provider/session execution (US-006 to US-009), cost accounting (US-010). A per-agent model or tool override inside chat is not added; the agent file and `agent.modelAliases` are the switches.

**Interface** — `ChatAgentRow` is `{ name, description, model, modelSource, tools: readonly string[] | "all", dropped }`; `ChatHost.agents?(): readonly ChatAgentRow[]`; `formatAgentsListing(rows)`.

Use resolveSubagentModel and mapSubagentTools rather than duplicating precedence or translations. An absent tools list is all; [] is none. Preserve shadowed resources using qualified names and catalog order. A host without agents() shows (no agents). The native host's current model must be read at listing time so inherited models follow switches; do not cache resolved rows at construction.

Required existing test update: packages/nax/test/ui/chat/slash-commands.test.tsx COMMANDS gains agents between mcp and quit; the contiguous /help expectation and parameterized AC-19 blocks /%s during turn then include /agents. Add the US-009 -> US-011 seam through runSlashCommand on a native host built by createChatHost with a fixture catalog agent, asserting show receives a line starting with the qualified agent name. Reuse the shared host harness rather than a mock agents() implementation for this integration seam.

routing.reasoning: A read-only host projection, formatter and built-in slash route reuse existing resolution helpers; no session lifecycle or permission enforcement changes, so simple TDD with the native-host seam and existing UI regression is sufficient.

analysis:
This is an additive enhancement to the existing native chat/resource architecture, not a greenfield agent implementation. Navigation used direct reads and text search because codebase-memory MCP was unavailable. The eleven-story decomposition and dependency graph are binding. Build order: US-001/002/003 independently; US-004 after 003; US-005 after 002; US-006 after 002/005; US-007 after 001/005; US-008 after 007; US-009 after 004/006/008; US-010 and US-011 after 009. Only US-001 edits nax-agent; all other implementation edits belong to packages/nax. No nax-ai or ACP changes, release, dependency additions, or version bumps are required.

Architecture and repository constraints: docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md:17 documents injectable _deps external-call seams and docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md:92 identifies prompts as a dedicated composition subsystem. Keep prompt literals in prompts/builders and compose host orchestration through a new subagent-runs module rather than growing chat-host. nax-agent must remain Node-compatible and use #src imports or explicit .ts relative imports; nax consumes its supported session APIs through @nathapp/nax-agent and must not import nax-ai here. Existing chat mode resolution is authoritative: packages/nax/src/chat/chat-mode.ts:12 maps guarded to ask/gated and full to full/raw; nested sessions consume that same resolved mode, not a separate agent permission profile. Do not add local permission fallbacks or reinterpret agent frontmatter permissions. Session, access-control, tool narrowing, ask routing and lifecycle stories use strict three-session-tdd. Unit/integration tests use bun:test and restored dependency seams rather than global module replacement. Show regression tests failing against old behavior before implementation. Run package-scoped commands, never bare bun test; do not run coverage inside NAX_SANDBOXED=1. Existing gates belong to the pipeline, not acceptance criteria.

US-001 findings: packages/nax-agent/src/session/native-backend-options.ts:18 defines NativeBackendOptions, and :73 starts a strict options schema that currently rejects allowedTools. Validation preserves the caller object rather than using Zod copies, so add shape validation without breaking identity. packages/nax-agent/src/session/session-tool-support.ts:31 defines profile declarations with universal scratchpads, :44 derives grants, :54 derives asks, and :158 builds coding support from that list. Filter profile tools before grants/asks, always retaining UNIVERSAL_CODING_TOOLS; never widen a profile. packages/nax-agent/src/session/native-backend.ts:79 currently resolves providers without admission options and :95 builds session tool support. packages/nax-agent/src/tools/provider-advertise.ts:103 already accepts admits; its :136 admission check occurs before adaptation, grants and ask collection, and :149 suppresses instructions when no provider tools survive. Reuse that existing seam for exact <id>__<tool> and <id>__* matches. Do not filter embedder tools. Existing tests include native-backend-options.test.ts, native-backend-providers.test.ts, session-tool-support.test.ts, native-backend.test.ts, agent-session-ask-profile.test.ts and session-interaction.test.ts under packages/nax-agent/test/unit/session. native-backend-providers.test.ts:50 provides a real backend-opening harness with memory transcripts; use its pattern rather than asserting only an isolated filter. Adding an option changes no exported type names, so the API dump should not change.

US-002 findings: packages/nax/src/resources/types.ts:38 declares AgentResource without prompt, :91 declares ResourceCatalog without agents/findAgent, while ResourcePackage already has agents. packages/nax/src/resources/parse-agent.ts:17 parses frontmatter but discards parsed.body; parse-skill.ts:30 retains parsed.body directly and is the reference for body fidelity. packages/nax/src/resources/catalog.ts:7 indexes only SkillResource | CommandResource; :35 builds indexes preserving package order and collision diagnostics. Extend this generic union and existing precedence rather than inventing a parallel agent lookup. The loader at catalog.ts:49 already delegates discovery to Claude package discovery and appends nax plugin packages, so discovery itself needs no new mechanism. packages/nax/src/resources/listing.ts:50 prints the deferred agent marker alongside the hooks marker; remove only the former. Required fixture migration: packages/nax/test/unit/resources/parse-agent.test.ts:9 and :45 whole-resource expectations gain prompt equal to Instructions, with the latter test renamed to reflect retained body; every other metadata expectation stays unchanged. packages/nax/test/unit/resources/listing.test.ts:28 agent literals gain prompt: empty string and :84 listing expectation loses only the agents marker. Extend existing catalog.test.ts, whose loadResourceCatalog tests start at :121, for fixture-repository discovery. Catalog changes also affect resources/skills-provider.ts, chat/resources.ts, slash commands, CLI resource loading and runtime resource consumers; most obtain catalogs through buildResourceCatalog and need no behavior change. Search typed literal mocks before editing because required catalog fields and prompt can surface type errors.

US-003/004 findings: packages/nax/src/config/schemas-infra.ts:464 declares AgentConfigSchema; schemas.ts:378 supplies a complete explicit agent default that must separately receive modelAliases: {} because that default is returned without parsing the nested object. packages/nax/src/config/runtime-types-agent.ts:204 is the handwritten runtime interface; config-descriptions.ts:374 begins related agent descriptions. Update all four surfaces, keeping modelAliases optional in the handwritten interface and defaulting it in both Zod paths. packages/nax-agent/src/native/models.ts:44 strips effort then splits the first slash; the alias validator additionally must reject whitespace as explicitly required by this spec. It must accept extra slashes in the model remainder and an optional effort suffix without requiring a catalog lookup or importing nax-ai. packages/nax/src/config/schemas-model.ts:207 and :219 show native tier entries may be objects or strings; preserve strings, compose object provider/model, and let aliases beat haiku/sonnet/opus tier defaults. Pure model/tool helpers belong in new chat files and are exported via packages/nax/src/chat/index.ts:1. Existing config tests to extend include test/unit/config/agent-schema.test.ts, schemas-infra.test.ts and schemas.test.ts. No persisted-config migration is necessary; {} preserves existing behavior. Tool-pattern removal is normalization, not enforcement: the whole mapped tool is granted and guarded asks still apply. Unknown entries drop without ever adding capabilities. Undefined tools and [] must remain distinguishable.

US-005/006 findings: packages/nax/src/prompts/builders/skills-builder/index.ts:7 builds the skills index; :13 performs whitespace collapse, C0/C1 removal, a second space collapse and truncation. Extract exactly that sequence into cleanIndexDescription so existing skills output stays byte-identical. packages/nax/src/prompts/builders/chat-builder.ts:17 builds chat instructions and :18 chooses permission sentences; preserve existing output, including headings and sandbox paragraph, when extracting chatPermissionParagraph. Reuse rules-index-builder and export the new agents builders from prompts/index.ts. Existing prompt tests are test/unit/prompts/builders/skills-builder.test.ts and chat-builder.test.ts. packages/nax/src/resources/skills-provider.ts:78 demonstrates a static provider with strict JSON schema, namespaced tool adaptation, injected resource lookup, instructions and bounded available-name errors. Mirror its pattern without loading agent instructions into the parent prompt. packages/nax/src/chat/chat-mcp.ts:27 reserves only nax-skills; :63 constructs the diagnostic and :100 filters the reserved server. Replace the single id with a set and parameterize the existing diagnostic so nax-skills wording/path/severity remain intact and nax-agents cannot be shadowed. Extend test/unit/chat/chat-mcp.test.ts while adding provider tests.

US-007/008 findings: packages/nax/src/chat/open-chat-session.ts:123 builds existing session options. Its rule lookup uses repoRoot for both repoRoot and packageDir plus configured overrideDir/overrideMode; :137 forwards catalogOverrides only when nonempty and compaction only when present; :140 composes nativeBackend including unsandboxed flags, carryHistoryAcrossModels, handlers and role. Mirror those options for subagents but use a fresh createMemoryTranscriptStore and omit storage metadata/locks/persistence. packages/nax-agent/src/session/agent-session-types.ts:53 defines facade options, :83 enumerates all five end statuses, :155 defines SessionEvent, and :168 defines AgentSession. send returns an AsyncIterable and claims the turn synchronously before its first next; close is idempotent and cancels/waits for a running turn. Wire onSession before starting send, handle throws both at send invocation and while iterating, preserve event order, and close in finally without leaking abort listeners. Resolve abort-before-create without allocating a session, and account for an abort while asynchronous creation is in progress. Only turn_end.output is final output; do not derive it from text deltas. packages/nax/src/context/rules/rule-delivery/index.ts:76 and :88 list eligible roles, :394 gates delivery, and :149 stores delivered identities per session name. Add subagent to both role arrays while sharing the host handler set; existing per-session tracking gives independent delivery. Existing rule-delivery.test.ts tests use toContain(tui), so the additive role should not alter their assertions. Scope US-007 to options and an immediate-end stub skeleton; US-008 completes results/cancellation/errors and rule delivery without creating a second runner.

US-009/010 findings: packages/nax/src/chat/resources.ts:7 already groups catalog, base toolProviders, pluginHandlers and teardown. packages/nax/src/chat/chat-host.ts:84 owns NativeChatHost; :120 currently routes every answer to the chat session. The three resource provider sites are :185 (start), :257 (resume) and :294 (reopen, including rollback). Compose a static agents provider only when agents exist, otherwise preserve the exact original array reference. current() is unreadable until a handle exists, so pass lazy current/ledger/turnListener closures when creating SubagentRuns and resolve current only inside run. The ledger is initialized lazily at chat-host.ts:199. packages/nax/src/chat/ask-controller.ts:44 handles approval/question events, performs full-mode and remembered auto-answer synchronously at :56, and preserves per-session approval memory; register requestId ownership before handing it an event. Prefix display reason/text on copies, not original events, and route answers to their nested session without changing controller options. Remove ownership on approval_resolved and runner completion. Nested sessions receive base resource providers only; never the nax-agents provider, including when tools is absent, making depth 1 structural.

The required host seam harness enters createChatHost without an open override, builds a real catalog, stubs _openChatSessionDeps.createAgentSession with a scripted parent, and captures _openChatSessionDeps.nativeBackend options. During parent send, discover nax-agents in those captured providers, await tools(cwd), then invoke run with agent/task and the turn AbortSignal. Drive the nested session via _subagentSessionDeps. Share this harness between US-009 and US-010; extend it for the US-011 slash seam instead of bypassing provider composition or calling helpers directly. packages/nax/test/unit/chat/chat-host-resources.test.ts:120 anchors original provider-array identity, :143 tests close/teardown ordering, and :225 demonstrates real opener seams. Preserve these tests unchanged. Keep seam restoration and temp fixtures in shared helpers.

packages/nax/src/chat/chat-ledger.ts:8 defines record(event, previousAt, model?) and :41 hardcodes sessionRole tui. Add the optional fourth role with tui default. Rewrite only the copied nested usage event sessionId to the parent id for the existing run-id grouping; record the resolved nested model and subagent role. Each nested invocation needs independent turn_start/previous usage timestamps so concurrent/nested calls do not share duration state. Accumulate turn_end spend separately from usage rows to avoid double-counting. packages/nax/src/chat/turn-runner.ts:9 defines options, :20 writes cumulative stored metadata, and :42 consumes a parent turn then drains the ledger. Read extraCostUsd once after a real turn_end, add it to that turn's cost, and keep calls without it unchanged. packages/nax/src/chat/chat-host.ts:327 wraps send; install and clear the event listener for exactly that send, and drain leftover nested cost in finally to prevent carryover after a throw. Only tool_call/tool_result reach the parent listener, not nested text, thinking, usage, asks, or turn boundaries. chat-host.ts:352 currently cancels only parent and :375 tears down parent before resources; extend to cancel nested work and await nested close before closing parent or MCP/resources. Preserve close idempotency, session-operation drains, lock ownership, rollback and teardown ordering. Existing test/unit/chat/turn-runner.test.ts:1 covers both ledger and runner using real temp storage and cost files. Extend it and host tests rather than changing default behavior.

US-011 findings: packages/nax/src/tui/chat/slash-commands.ts:26 holds the built-in order and :107 handles mcp; add agents between mcp and quit with optional-host fallback. /cost already reads host.current().meta.costUsd, so US-010 metadata accounting automatically includes nested spend. packages/nax/src/chat/chat-host.ts:34 defines optional resources on ChatHost; add optional agents() to avoid breaking existing UI hosts. Add chat-agents-listing.ts and exports in chat/index.ts, formatting all catalog agents in order and resolving current model at listing time. packages/nax/test/ui/chat/slash-commands.test.tsx:11 has a parallel COMMANDS fixture that must gain agents between mcp and quit; its host fixture at :51 omits optional APIs and must continue to work. Existing chat-mcp-listing.ts is the formatting reference. Build a native-host runSlashCommand seam with a real catalog in addition to pure formatter tests.

Risk and migration summary: primary hazards are accidentally widening tool permissions, filtering after grants, losing universal scratchpads, allowing nested agents through inherited providers, misrouting synchronous full-mode auto-approvals, leaking sessions or AbortSignal listeners, persisting ephemeral subagents, deadlocking close, and charging nested spend twice or carrying failed-send spend into another send. Undefined allowedTools must preserve current backend behavior exactly; unknown tool names do not add tools; unknown model labels fall back visibly rather than fail. The API changes are additive except required prompt/catalog properties in internal resource literals, which need narrowly scoped fixture updates described above. Existing skills/chat prompt outputs, no-agent array identity, hooks wording, original reserved-id diagnostic, default tui cost rows, and existing metadata accumulation are explicit regression anchors. No database/transcript migration is needed: only parent metadata/cost rows persist and nested transcripts stay memory-only. Feature completion means a real host send can invoke a catalog agent through nax-agents__run, inherit current permissions, narrow declarations, resolve its model, route human asks, deliver rules, return final text, account usage/cost, clean up on failure/cancellation, and expose /agents. Keep .nax context/manual design-status updates and nax generate outside implementation stories; only this requested PRD artifact is written here.

Second-pass adversarial audit: enumerated all 190 explicit spec ACs against their original story and ordinal: US-001 18, US-002 13, US-003 9, US-004 19, US-005 15, US-006 22, US-007 20, US-008 19, US-009 21, US-010 17, US-011 17. None were dropped or moved. Exact regression anchors remain: US-001 as before this change; US-005 same text as before this change for skills and both chat modes; US-006 injected ToolResult unchanged and nax-skills still reserved; US-007 loopHandlers identity and absent allowedTools key; US-008 tui Write behavior; US-009 no-agent provider-array identity and the full-mode host-routing parenthetical; US-010 default tui rows and no-extra-cost behavior; US-011 turn blocking like every other built-in. No deprecated grep/file/verbatim AC tags exist. Public-export checks now exercise callable exports or a typed-row formatter consumer; prompt-regression ACs freeze literal expected output rather than comparing the new helper with itself. The rule-handler AC states the observable unseen-rule Write block and compares content against a fresh equivalent tui handler state.

Every story has a negative path: invalid options/undeclared Write (001), missing agent lookup and collisions (002), malformed aliases (003), unknown model/tool and Agent/Task dropping (004), control-character rejection from index output (005), malformed/unknown provider input and reserved MCP collision (006), backend-option-construction throw preventing creation plus explicit empty restriction preservation (007), throw/abort/non-completed status cleanup (008), cancellation and prevention of nested-provider/answer misrouting (009), failed-send accounting isolation and cancellation/close (010), unknown model/tool display, optional-host fallback and turn blocking (011). outOfScope: Subagents in `nax run` are not supported; the agents provider attaches to `nax chat` only.
Subagent depth is 1: a nested session never receives the `nax-agents` provider, and an agent's `Agent` or `Task` tool entry is dropped.

Nested sessions are not persisted: they use an in-memory transcript store, are not listed by `/sessions`, and cannot be resumed; a resumed chat session does not restore a subagent that was running when the process died.

Claude Code agent frontmatter other than `name`, `description`, `model` and `tools` (for example `color`, `permissionMode`, `hooks`, `skills`) is ignored; a subagent always runs in the chat session's current mode.
Narrowing a subagent's mode below the chat session's (for example a read-only profile for an agent whose tools are all read-only) is not done; the tool narrowing is the only narrowing.
A Claude Code tool pattern such as `Bash(git diff:*)` is not enforced; the entry grants the whole tool and the existing guarded asks still apply to every call.
Embedder tools (`CreateAgentSessionOptions.tools`) are not filtered by `allowedTools`.

Claude Code plugin MCP tool names of the form `mcp__plugin_<plugin>_<server>__<tool>` are not translated to nax's `<plugin>-<server>` server ids; such an entry maps to `plugin_<plugin>_<server>__<tool>` and matches nothing.
The transcript shows a subagent's tool calls and results only; its streamed text and thinking are not shown, and its final text appears as the `nax-agents__run` tool result.
Background (non-blocking) subagents are not supported; a `nax-agents__run` call returns when the nested turn ends.
A per-agent model or tool override inside chat is not added; the agent file and `agent.modelAliases` are the switches.
Agents are not hot-reloaded; a changed agent file takes effect at the next `nax chat` start.
Hooks stay parsed and listed as not executed.

Updating `.nax/mono/packages/nax/context.md` and `.nax/mono/packages/nax-agent/context.md` for subagents and `allowedTools`, then running `nax generate`, is a manual step after merge; `.nax/` is read-only to the run.
